transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Ever since an armed robbery I went through about two years ago, I keep organizing my whole life around avoiding anything that reminds me of it—certain neighborhoods, late meetings, even some community events. It has just gotten to the point where I'm arranging my entire schedule around trying to feel safe.
Have these symptoms of avoidance and distress been present for less than six months, or have they persisted for six months or longer since the robbery?
They have definitely been going on for much longer than six months. They actually started a few months after the robbery and have been happening steadily for well over a year now.

latest_inference.note: The patient confirmed that the symptoms have persisted for significantly longer than six months, which allows us to rule out the acute form (F43.10) and the delayed-onset form (F43.12) as the primary classification. F43.11 (Chronic) is now the most appropriate diagnosis given the duration of over one year.
